lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: US HRC spot kept rising after the July guide was set. Nucor's consumer spot price was $1,130-1,135/st in July (SMU 2026-07-06/13/20), $1,160 on 2026-08-10, $1,190 on 2026-09-08, $1,220 by 2026-09-28 and +$10 again on 2026-10-05. Kallanish had domestic HRC at $1,210-1,220/st on 2026-09-25 against $825-865 a year earlier. Lead times are stretched. Cliffs' Q3 guide assumed only about +$55/t ASP over Q2's $1,124 and +300kt of shipments. So the spot-linked and monthly-index part of the book supports Q3 at or slightly above $575m, and a Q4 guide above the implied ~$725m consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is what this name trades on. 2026-07-23 rose +15.98% on the Q3 $575m guide despite an EPS miss. 2025-10-20 rose +21.47%. 2026-02-09 fell -16.43% on a miss and a weak outlook.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-06 Wells Fargo (Tanners) upgraded CLF to Overweight with a $14 target. The note says 2H26 and 2027 EBITDA will 'materially exceed' consensus: 2027 at $2.65B against roughly $2.3B consensus, even if HRC falls to about $1,000/st. Named drivers are repricing about 2Mt/yr of open fixed-price contracts (~$500m), lower discounts on about 6Mt of CRU-linked contracts (~$240m), and Stelco pricing. Last October's call carried the fixed-price contract resets, and management already said in July that 2027 resets are higher.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 2025 print (2025-10-20) rose +21.47% when management discussed contract renegotiations and the forward outlook. 2026-07-23 rose +15.98% on forward commentary.

findings.finding: Peer pre-guides set after Cliffs last spoke point to strong Q3 flat-rolled pricing with mixed beats. Steel Dynamics (2026-09-17) guided Q3 EPS to $5.34-5.38, against $3.69 in Q2, on record steel shipments, wider metal margins, higher realised prices and low customer inventories, with automotive among the solid end markets. Nucor (2026-09-17) guided $5.55-5.65, below a ~$5.99-6.17 consensus, but its steel mills earned more on higher selling prices with stable volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No CLF-specific history on a peer read-through. CLF's Q3 is itself pre-guided, so the reported quarter alone has rarely moved it; the guide has.

findings.finding: Stelco/Ottawa dispute. On 2026-09-29 Cliffs announced it would indefinitely idle cold-rolled and coated lines at Hamilton (wind-down from 10-09, up to 500 jobs; Stelco demand fell about 25% in Q2 2026 against the 2024 average). Ottawa says this breaches the 2024 Investment Canada Act undertakings: Joly's letter of 10-05 gave five business days and threatened a court order, penalties or a forced sale. Stelco replied that it is not in breach and the layoffs proceed. Goncalves said he is ready for court and would sell Stelco 'for a good offer'. CLF fell 9% on 09-28 and 4% on 10-15 while NUE and STLD fell about 1-2%. The call will have to address it, along with any idling charges.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print on a Stelco legal dispute. The headline days themselves moved CLF -9% (2026-09-28) and -4% (2026-10-15) against its peers, so the stock is sensitive to this line between prints.

findings.finding: Management said about half of the +300kt Q3 shipment step-up would come from automotive. Omdia's North America production tracker has Q3 2026 output pacing down about 0.6% (July +5.4% on the model-year 2027 start), with Mexico losing ground. That is a modest risk to the auto half of the volume assumption.
findings.source_date: 2026-08 (Omdia tracker, July data; paywalled, headline/summary only)
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Auto weakness drove the weak 2H24 prints. The volume miss on 2026-02-09 coincided with -16.43%.

findings.finding: Canada doubled its counter-surtax on affected US-origin steel goods from 25% to 50% effective 2026-09-08 (C$4.57B of basic and semi-finished steel). That raises the cost of Cliffs' US-mill shipments into Canada in late Q3 and Q4, while further shielding Stelco's domestic market.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for this line specifically. Trade-policy days moved CLF more than its peers (09-28, 10-15).

findings.finding: Positioning into the print favours upside asymmetry. 13.89% of float is short (4.7 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-30); call skew is -15.6 vol points; the stock fell 6.3% in the five sessions before the print on headline risk; only about 25% of analysts rate it Buy. A guide or contract-reset surprise meets a crowded short.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Large upside moves on forward-looking beats (+15.98%, +21.47%, +12.45%) came with similarly elevated short interest.

outside_window.finding: Steel Dynamics reports Q3 after the close on 2026-10-19, and Nucor on 2026-10-26. Read-throughs from those calls land after CLF's exit window.
Any Canadian superior-court application under the Investment Canada Act, seeking penalties or a forced sale of Stelco, has no filing date; none had been filed as of 2026-10-11.
The POSCO strategic partnership remains an MOU. The definitive-agreement timeline has slipped past 1H26 and management says it is not in a hurry.

findings.finding: Long rates rose sharply in Q3 2026: the 10-year was 5.11% on 2026-09-23, and a WSJ summary put the quarter's rise at about 85bp, the largest since 2016. Peers that have reported show the tangible-book hit: Regions TBVPS fell 8.2% q/q ($13.78 to $12.65), Citizens fell 6.6% ($38.29 to $35.78, which it attributed to 'higher long-term rates on the investment securities and swap portfolios'), and Citizens cut its Q3 buyback to $125m from $225m. FITB entered Q3 with a $2.9bn after-tax unrealized loss and CET1 including AOCI of about 8.7%, while regulatory CET1 was 9.9% against a 10-10.5% target. FITB's own 6/30 slide projected AOCI improving to -$2.7bn by year-end, which the rate move reverses. The Street expects a $200-300m Q4 buyback, and the risk is that the call delays or shrinks it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved FITB print in the baseline turned on capital return; buybacks were paused all of H1 2026 after the Comerica close. Peers on the same AOCI line this week: Regions +2.3% on its print with TBV -8.2% and a $95m buyback; Citizens about -1.0% intraday with TBV -6.6% and a smaller buyback.

Deposit-cost drift after the September hike was small (Regions interest-bearing deposit costs +1bp, Citizens +5bp). Same-day stock reactions were mixed: USB +2.0% (10-15), PNC -0.4% while KRE rose 1.8% (10-15), RF +2.3%, TFC +1.1%, CFG -1.0% and MTB -2.7% intraday on 10-16.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FITB's own credit line has been quiet since the 2025 Tricolor impairment ($170-200m, Q3 2025); Q2 2026 NCOs of 30bp were the lowest since 2Q23, and the stock still fell on that print.

findings.finding: The Comerica systems conversion (about 600,000 accounts, 293 branches, Labor Day weekend 2026) produced local-news reports on 2026-09-08/09 of login lockouts, bill-pay outages of up to eight days, cancelled autopays and long hold times in Michigan and Texas. A week later management said it was 'as close to perfect as I have seen', with inbound calls 15% below the MB Financial conversion, commercial gross attrition under 1%, consumer attrition 'very stable and very muted', and 'quite a strong quarter' for deposit growth. Q3 period-end deposits and retention figures will show which account holds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior FITB print turned on deposit attrition; Q2 commercial retention was 99.4% and the stock fell 2.29% on other lines.

findings.finding: Cost synergies are running above the formal target: on 2026-09-15 the COO said 'we hit the $850 million' and the CFO said 'we're probably north of $900 million at this point'. Management also guides to more than $500m of revenue synergies over 3-5 years and a 53% efficiency target for 2027. The Q3 call is the first with the conversion done, so a formal raise of the $850m run-rate target and a first 2027 expense outlook are likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 raised NII and fee guidance and cut expense guidance, and the stock fell 2.29%, so guide raises on this name have not reliably paid.

findings.finding: FITB goes into the print on a sector de-rating, not a company-specific one. The KBW Bank Index fell 13% from mid-August and September was financials' worst month against the S&P 500 since 1990, which Truist's Foran attributed to fund flows rather than results. Over 20 sessions FITB fell 4.9% against KRE's 4.3%, and it is 15% off its 52-week high. Four sell-side target cuts landed 09-23 to 10-05 with no rating changes. Short interest rose 13% in the second half of September, to 36.3M shares (5.0 days to cover).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior FITB print came into a comparable sector drawdown in the baseline window. Peers this week coming off the same drawdown were mixed on the day (RF +2.3%, USB +2.0%, TFC +1.1%, PNC -0.4%, CFG -1.0%, MTB -2.7%).

findings.finding: Industry commercial loan demand is strong: the Fed's H.8 shows C&I loans growing about 18.8% annualized in August 2026 (12.0% July, 14.8% June) and bank credit about 4.8%. FITB guided Q3 average loans to only +1% and on 09-15 said loans were 'coming in as expected' and Comerica loans 'relatively stable'. FITB's middle-market sales force is 75% larger after Comerica, so there is scope for a firmer Q4 loan guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loan growth has not been the line FITB's reactions were attributed to in the resolved prints.

findings.finding: Q3 NIM will be flat or down against Q2's 3.36%: management said it 'sticks in the mid-330s' because cash balances ran 'north of $20 billion' for most of the quarter. Contributors were about $2bn of Comerica sweep balances placed on deposit during the transition and a Southwest deposit campaign that beat its $2.5bn target by more than double; promotional deposits are higher-cost funding. The 3.40% exit-rate target therefore rests on Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 NIM rose 6bp to 3.36% and the stock still fell 2.29%; Truist was 'dinged on NIM concern' in Q2 per Zacks, so the sector does punish NIM misses.

findings.finding: Liability housekeeping in the quarter: a registered exchange of $1.27bn of Comerica-era restricted senior notes (4.000% 2029 and 5.982% FtF 2030) settled about 2026-09-24 with 99.9%+ tendered and no P&L effect stated, and the full $500m 1.707% FtF senior notes due 2027 are called at par for 2026-11-01. Asked what the money buys: nothing new. These are a registration change and a routine call of low-coupon paper, funded from the $20bn-plus cash position.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none

findings.finding: The rate deck has not moved against the guide. FITB's FY and Q3 NII guidance assumed a 4.00% fed funds rate at both 9/30 and 12/31, and the upper bound was 4.00% on 2026-09-30 after the September hike. FITB is mildly asset-sensitive (+0.4% NII in year 1 and +1.9% in year 2 for +100bp). Higher long rates lift fixed-rate asset repricing, which Regions and Citizens both cited as a NII driver. Together that is a modest tailwind for the 2027 NII outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 NII guide raise was sold (-2.29%).

Next FOMC meeting on 2026-10-27/28, with the market pricing a low (about 19%) probability of another hike; this would move FITB's rate assumptions only after the window.
